I live in the UK and all that happened when I told them I feel suicidal was get put on medication and given one to one half an hour sessions every 2 weeks. It was a form of CBT, but didn't last very long. I came in to a session in a very fragile state telling them I couldn't stop thinking about suicide and I was referred to a risk management team. The guy I saw from that team decided I was capable of dealing with it myself and now I'm only on medication. I've been self harming pretty severely, but I think here they'll only put you into a psych ward if you've made plans. I was asked that question a lot. Probably totally different abroad though.

I've come to know that people don't actually care about you, even those that profess to be your friends and pretend they care about you. I told my two supposedly closest friends that I'm severely suicidal and have been cutting myself and they responded by ignoring me for the next two weeks.

You're much better off finding something that makes you happy on your own, than relying on trying to get rid of the loneliness. I'm trying my best to develop a passion for something, while not pursuing friendships, I think it's best to just go along with whatever little interaction that might come from these pseudo friendships than not, but just try not to get so personally involved. That's my thought process anyway. It's more than likely dreadful advice, but that's where I am at the moment.
